data.claim: Lease.live includes grace, remaining_s ignores it, so inside grace the refusal prints a negative number
data.falsifier: refusal text has no negative number inside grace
data.mechanism: acquire raises 'held by .. for another {remaining_s}s' whenever live() is true
data.probe_output: fails on unfixed code (negative countdown), passes fixed
data.question: Why does claim print a negative countdown?

evidence.note: read brief lessons; none constrain the message change
leases.py message + test_lease_api regression test; 14 passed

chunk_findings.detail:
The new refusal text tells the caller to run `ddflow claim {item_id} --force`:

```
f"its {cfg.lease.grace_s}s grace period; it can be taken over "
f"(`ddflow recover --item {item_id}`, then `ddflow claim {item_id} --force`) "
```

`claim` has no `--force` flag — as the change's own intent statement records ("claim --force is not an option, release --force is") and as D-lease-break-explicit records ("an idle contended lease is broken only by `ddflow claim --break`"). Concrete scenario: holder H's lease on item T1 is past TTL, inside grace; a second agent runs `ddflow claim T1`, hits this branch, and copies the printed command. `ddflow claim T1 --force` exits with an unknown-option error, so the agent is still stuck with no way forward — exactly the symptom the bug is supposed to remove. The message must name `--break` (and/or the auto-break config) instead of a non-existent `--force`. [D-lease-break-explicit]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:287 (the new grace-period branch of `acquire`)

chunk_findings.detail: The message promises automatic takeover after the grace window elapses: `in {cfg.lease.grace_s + left:.0f}s`. With the project default `[lease].break_on_timeout = false` (D-lease-break-explicit), nothing breaks the lease when the grace runs out; a later claimant still cannot take an idle contended lease without the explicit `ddflow claim --break`. So for the default configuration the printed countdown is false — an agent can sit waiting past the advertised time and still be refused. Either the branch should only print the countdown when automatic break is enabled, or it should state that `--break` is required. [D-lease-break-explicit]

titles: ddflow/services/leases.py:290 (the "can be taken over in Ns" countdown)

chunk_findings.detail: The new "way forward" the message advertises is not runnable: it tells the user to run `ddflow claim {item_id} --force`, but `--force` is not an option on `claim` (`release --force` is; the documented explicit break path is `ddflow claim --break`). Input that demonstrates it: a holder has a lease 76s past its TTL and still inside the grace window, a second party runs `ddflow claim T1` and gets the new text `... (`ddflow recover --item T1`, then `ddflow claim T1 --force`) in Ns`. Acting on it, `ddflow claim T1 --force` fails at argument parsing with an "unrecognized arguments: --force" error, so the message replaces one dead end (the `-76s` countdown) with another dead end. This also contradicts the recorded decision [D-lease-break-explicit], which states that an idle contended lease is broken only by `ddflow claim --break` (automatic breaking is off by default); the message never mentions `--break`, and by default the lease is *not* "taken over" when the grace window elapses, so the promise "it can be taken over ... in {grace_s + left}s" is itself only true if the user first uses the break path. Note also that the change leaves the refusal itself untouched — `acquire` still raises for the expired-in-grace lease — so if the bug report is that the claim refuses, only the wording changed. The regression test in tests/test_lease_api.py:81 asserts the message contains `grace period` and `ddflow recover --item T1` but never checks that the suggested command is a valid invocation, so it passes on a message that cannot be followed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:292 (the new grace-period message)

data.probe: ddflow claim --help lists --force (takeover of an expired lease); --break is for live idle leases. Refusal inside grace is by design (lease.grace_s doc); only the nonsensical countdown was the defect
